principles.statement: Multi-start simulated annealing with greedy local search achieves ~85% cut ratio on Max-Cut instances with n<=1000, m<=20000, far exceeding the ~50% random baseline.
principles.regime: Undirected graphs with n<=1000, m<=20000, single-vertex-flip neighborhood
principles.mechanism: Greedy local search reaches local optima (~80% cut ratio). SA with slow cooling (alpha=0.99997) escapes shallow local optima via probabilistic acceptance of worsening moves. Multi-start (20 restarts) diversifies initial conditions. Re-greedy after SA polishes the SA solution.
principles.applicability_bounds: Holds for sparse-to-moderate density graphs within the stated size bounds. May not scale to n>>1000 due to fixed iteration counts. The ~85% score is near the Goemans-Williamson 0.878 approximation bound, suggesting diminishing returns from SA alone.

principles.statement: Do not use chrono/clock-based timing in Frontier-CS judge solutions — use fixed iteration counts instead.
principles.mechanism: The designer observed that chrono::steady_clock-based loop control caused score=0, likely due to judge environment restrictions or overhead. Fixed iteration counts with tuned alpha work reliably.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to all Frontier-CS algorithmic problems. May not apply to other judges.
